exegra.doc: Schema version of the specification format.

vocabulary.doc: Model-defined extensions of categories, relationship kinds and properties.

logical.label: Logical module
logical.description: A logical unit of responsibility with no declared runtime of its own.

computational.label: Computational service
computational.description: An executing process or service that performs computation.

storage.label: Data store
storage.description: A component whose responsibility is durable or shared state.

external.label: External system
external.description: A system outside the control of the specified system.

infrastructure.label: Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Platform, transport, tooling or operational substrate.

transport.label: Message transport
transport.description: An asynchronous channel carrying messages between components.

depends-on.label: Depends on
depends-on.description: The source requires the target to fulfil its responsibilities.

calls.label: Calls
calls.description: The source synchronously invokes an operation of the target.

data-flow.label: Data flow
data-flow.description: Data moves from source to target. Says nothing about who initiates.

publishes.label: Publishes
publishes.description: The source asynchronously emits messages to the target channel.

subscribes.label: Subscribes
subscribes.description: The source consumes messages from the target channel.

reads.label: Reads
reads.description: The source reads state held by the target.

writes.label: Writes
writes.description: The source mutates state held by the target.

observes.label: Observes
observes.description: The source collects telemetry about the target.

system.label: System
system.doc: The top-level specification and its metadata.

illustrative.label: Illustrative
illustrative.doc: True when the whole system is an example and not a description of real software.

generation.label: Generation
generation.doc: Setting it declares the specification ready to generate code from: the readiness rules (src/core/readiness.js, codes ready.*) become errors. Without it they are only listed by the readiness command.

target.label: Target
target.doc: The language to generate, such as rust.

functionBranches.label: Function branches
functionBranches.doc: How ready.function-branch-uncovered (a branch of a function that no example takes, docs/coverage.md) is reported: error (the default) or gap, listed with severity info while the examples are being completed.

wireCase.label: Wire case
wireCase.doc: How generated code names the JSON members of contract inputs, outputs and errors, of the struct types they use (transitively) and of event payloads a contract carries. The specification keeps kebab-case names; the generator converts. Defaults to kebab-case (the names as written). A contract may override it with binding.case.

errorKinds.label: Error kinds
errorKinds.doc: {kind: HTTP status}: the kinds of failure a contract error may name in errors[].kind, each with the status it is answered with (an integer from 400 to 599).

errorStatus.label: Default error status
errorStatus.doc: The HTTP status of a contract error that states neither status nor kind. Without it (and without errorKind) such an error is a readiness gap.

errorKind.label: Default error kind
errorKind.doc: The kind of a contract error that states neither status nor kind; a key of errorKinds. Not together with errorStatus.

errorBody.label: Error body
errorBody.doc: The body every failed call is answered with, instead of the runtime's own: a struct type whose code field holds the kind of the failure, with the message and correlation fields named and every other field optional; runtime maps each failure the serving runtime reports itself to an error kind.

type.doc: The struct type of the body.

code.doc: The field that holds the error kind: an enum whose values include every key of errorKinds.

message.doc: The string field that holds a message safe to show the caller.

correlation.doc: The string field that holds the caller's correlation id, which the route fills in.

runtime.doc: {runtime failure: error kind} for unauthenticated, forbidden, invalid-request, timeout, unavailable and internal.

retry.label: Retry policy
retry.doc: How the generated runtime retries an at-least-once message whose dispatch failed: the wait after the first failure, the factor each further failure multiplies it by, and the longest wait. Defaults to the runtime's own policy: 1 s, factor 2, at most 300 s. Exegra's retry-event delays and the delays fault.unrealisable accepts for an at-least-once event are sums of these waits.

max.label: Longest wait
max.doc: A duration of at least the first wait.

gateway.label: Gateway
gateway.doc: The gateway public contracts are routed through.

prefix.doc: The path every route through the gateway is under, such as /api. Only a public contract may be bound under it.

developmentConditions.label: Development conditions
developmentConditions.doc: The deployment conditions under which development and fixture contracts exist, such as STRATA_DEV.

telemetry.label: Telemetry
telemetry.doc: The services whose generated code writes structured logs, one JSON object per line: ts (milliseconds since the Unix epoch), level, service, event (the log name), correlation and tenant when known, then the logged event's allowlisted fields. Which events each service logs is stated on the event (logging). docs/model-and-format.md, "Telemetry".

format.label: Format
format.doc: The line format; json-lines is the only one, and the default.

id.label: Service
id.doc: The service name written on every line.

component.label: Component
component.doc: The component that runs as this service.

log.label: Log file
log.doc: Where the deployment keeps the service's log, relative to its working directory, such as var/logs/backend.jsonl. End-to-end tests read it.

component.label: Component
component.doc: A logical, computational, storage, client, external or infrastructure entity. kind 'subsystem' marks a component that contains other components.

kind.label: Kind
kind.doc: Defaults to component. Only a subsystem may be the parent of other components.

trustZone.label: Trust zone
trustZone.doc: Name of the trust boundary this component lives inside.

language.label: Language
language.doc: The language the component's logic is implemented in; mixed when its modules span more than one.

trusts.label: Trusted base
trusts.doc: Assumptions the correctness of this implementation rests on and nothing checks: compilers, runtimes, platforms.

port.label: Port
port.doc: An explicitly declared interaction surface of a component.

relationship.label: Relationship
relationship.doc: A typed, directed connection between components or ports.

contract.label: Contract
contract.doc: Inputs, outputs, preconditions, postconditions, error conditions and obligations of an interaction.

encode.label: Encoding
encode.doc: How a page's request turns the value it holds into what the endpoint takes, in this order: trim (true: white space removed at both ends), split (a separator: the text becomes the list of its trimmed, non-empty parts), as (number: the text becomes a number), empty (null: an empty value, meaning an empty text, an empty list or false, is sent as null; omit: it is left out of the request).

type.doc: The type of the error payload, when it carries one.

status.label: HTTP status
status.doc: The HTTP status the error is answered with, an integer from 400 to 599. State this or kind, not both.

kind.label: Error kind
kind.doc: The kind of failure, a key of system.generation.errorKinds; the error is answered with the status of its kind, and an error body carries the kind as its code.

case.label: Wire case
case.doc: Overrides system.generation.wireCase for this contract: the JSON names of its inputs, outputs, errors and the types they reach.

suppliedBy.label: Supplied inputs
suppliedBy.doc: Input name -> route or session: an input the request address (route) or the signed-in session supplies. It is never read from the request body, and a body that carries it is refused.

ref.label: Reference
ref.doc: A stable code for the contract, such as CT-012; for a hand-written contract (a hole) H-012, the code its implementation names in an Implements line.

realisation.label: Realisation
realisation.doc: target: specified but not yet implemented; a generator emits the contract's types and a trait method with no implementation and serves no route for it, and nothing may call it through a derivation or a facade. generated: the code is generated from this contract. hand: a hole, written by hand against its postconditions. derived: the implementation is generated from its derivation (functions, and the contracts it loads and commits through). facade: no server implementation; the client lowers it onto the generic contract its bffRoute names (docs/model-and-format.md, "Derived and facade contracts").

derivation.label: Derivation
derivation.doc: A derived contract's implementation. pure: {kind, function}. read: {kind, needs, load, decide}, optionally with insufficient and needRounds: ask again while decide fails with insufficient, as a command does, without a commit. command: {kind, needs, load, decide, commit, conflict, insufficient, needRounds, retries}: load what needs says, decide, ask again while decide fails with insufficient (at most needRounds extra rounds), commit, and start over while the commit fails with conflict (at most retries times). Each kind may name fault, the contract error an integer overflow in a function becomes.

function.label: Function
function.doc: pure: the function that is the contract's implementation.

needs.label: Needs
needs.doc: read, command: the function that gives the list of needs to load, from the contract's inputs.

load.label: Load
load.doc: read, command: the contract that loads the needs.

decide.label: Decide
decide.doc: read, command: the function that decides from the inputs and what was loaded.

commit.label: Commit
commit.doc: command: the contract that commits what decide gives.

conflict.label: Conflict error
conflict.doc: command: the error of the commit contract that means another commit got there first.

insufficient.label: Insufficient-state error
insufficient.doc: command, and optionally read: the variant of decide's error union that asks for one more need (a newtype variant of the need type).

needRounds.label: Need rounds
needRounds.doc: command, and a read that names insufficient: how many extra needs one decision may ask for.

retries.label: Conflict retries
retries.doc: command: how often a commit that lost a race is decided again.

header.label: Header step
header.doc: read, command: true when the load contract is first called with no needs (the header: what every load holds), its outputs are available to the needs function as parameters, and the needs it gives are then loaded together in one round that does not count against needRounds.

fault.label: Fault error
fault.doc: The error of this contract that an integer overflow or a division by zero in a function becomes; a generator refuses a function that can fault without it.

implementedBy.label: Implemented by
implementedBy.doc: The component whose code implements the contract.

deployment.label: Deployment
deployment.doc: shipped: the contract is served by code that exists. target: it describes what the enterprise product will serve. Default: target when implementedBy names a component with implementation.status not-implemented, otherwise shipped. An explicit shipped on a not-implemented component is contract.deployment-subject. (Named deployment, not realisation, because contract.realisation is generated or hand.)

auth.label: Authorisation
auth.doc: Who may call it, in the specification's own words.

auth.label: Authorisation
auth.doc: Who may call it: {scheme, requires?, roles?, policies?, tenantPolicies?, csrf?, origin?, stepUp?, secret?, justification?, description?}, requires the ids of the capabilities a call needs, scheme one of anonymous, session, service, provisioning-token, signature, signed-address, delegation, in-process (docs/model-and-format.md#contract-exposure-and-auth). A sentence is accepted only without system.generation.

exposure.label: Exposure
exposure.doc: Where the contract can be reached from: public (browsers and the internet, through the gateway), internal (the service network only) or local (an in-process call, never a route).

readOnly.label: Read-only
readOnly.doc: True when a call changes no state. A public contract that is not read-only needs a session with CSRF and origin checked, or a verified credential.

tenantScope.label: Tenant scope
tenantScope.doc: What tenant data it reads and returns: request (only the tenant the request is made in, which a principal's own tenant must match), none, or platform (across tenants; never on a public contract).

development.label: Development condition
development.doc: For a development or fixture contract: the deployment condition (one of system.generation.developmentConditions) without which it does not exist.

idempotent.label: Idempotent
idempotent.doc: True when repeating a call has the effect of making it once.

timeoutMs.label: Timeout (ms)
timeoutMs.doc: A positive integer: how long a caller waits.

milestone.label: Milestone
milestone.doc: For a hand-written contract (a hole): the milestone whose start makes its implementation expected, like a requirement's milestone.

policyDefault.label: Policy default
policyDefault.doc: What the policies on this contract decide when no policy matches: deny (refuse) or allow. A matching deny policy always refuses, and a matching allow permits unless a deny matches too.

event.label: Event
event.doc: An occurrence that can trigger transitions.

sensitive.label: Sensitive
sensitive.doc: The kind of sensitive data the field holds; it is never logged.

delivery.label: Delivery
delivery.doc: Implementation level: the delivery guarantee of an emitted event. Declarative; simulation ignores it (docs/semantics.md).

elapsed.label: Elapsed time
elapsed.doc: Implementation level: the event represents elapsed time and must be the emit of some timer effect. Declarative; simulation ignores it.

domain.label: Domain event
domain.doc: The event is a fact the running system records (a domain event). With system.generation set, a domain event must state its logging (ready.event-logging-missing).

logging.label: Logging
logging.doc: Whether generated code logs the event, and what its line holds: {logged: true, service, level, name?, tenant?, fields: [{field, as?}]} or {logged: false, reason}. Logging is an allowlist; a payload is never logged whole, and a sensitive field never. docs/model-and-format.md, "Telemetry".

service.label: Service
service.doc: A service of system.telemetry whose log holds the event.

name.label: Log name
name.doc: The event member of the line, such as record.updated. Defaults to the event id.

tenant.label: Tenant field
tenant.doc: The payload field written as the line's tenant.

as.label: Written as
as.doc: The member name in the line; defaults to the field name.

reason.label: Reason
reason.doc: Why an event that is not logged is not.

behavior.label: Behavior
behavior.doc: A state machine describing how one component reacts to events.

repr.label: Representation type
repr.doc: Implementation level: a built-in representation type (src/core/builtin-types.js), a declared type, or list<T> / option<T>. Declarative; simulation ignores it.

instances.label: Instances
instances.doc: Format 2: {count} or {key, max}. Implementation level: {key, storedIn}, where storedIn is a record whose key field is `key` (declarative; the simulation input drops storedIn).

level.label: Level
level.doc: model (default) or implementation: an implementation-level machine is held to the rules of src/core/readiness-machines.js. Declarative; simulation ignores it.

realisation.label: Realisation
realisation.doc: shipped: the machine models code that exists. target: it models what the enterprise product will have, not what is built. Default: target when the subject component has implementation.status not-implemented, otherwise shipped. An explicit shipped on a not-implemented subject is behavior.realisation-subject. Declarative; simulation ignores it (docs/semantics.md).

storage.label: Storage
storage.doc: Implementation level: the record that holds this machine's state and the key field that identifies a machine in it. Declarative; the simulation input drops it, like instances.storedIn.

durability.label: Durability
durability.doc: record (default): the machine is held in a record, storage.record and storage.key say which, and a transaction is declared. memory: the instance lives in process memory for a connection or tab, so no record, key, fields, state, stateValues, creates, instances.storedIn or transaction is declared (storage.durability, docs/semantics.md). Declarative; simulation ignores it.

key.label: Key field
key.doc: Required when durability is record (storage.durability). The record's whole key: one field name when the key is one field, or the list of every key field in the record's order when it is composite (storage.key-whole). A key that names part of the record's key is an error: records that agree on that part would share one instance.

fields.label: Variable fields
fields.doc: {variable: record field}: the record field that holds each variable. A variable not listed is held in the field of the same name.

state.label: State field
state.doc: The record field that holds the control state, default "state": a required string or enum field.

stateValues.label: State values
stateValues.doc: {state id: stored value}: what the state field holds for each state, when it is not the state id (for an enum field whose values are named otherwise). Values are distinct.

creates.label: Creates records
creates.doc: True when an event for a key with no record creates the record; the machine must then fill every required field. Default false: the machine steps only records that already exist and carries the fields it does not hold over from them.

createdBy.label: Created by
createdBy.doc: For a machine that does not create its records: the contract whose call writes the record, with the machine in its initial state, before the machine's first event. Until then the runtime refuses the machine's events (RecordMissing). A shipped machine that a scenario runs needs creates or createdBy (machine.initial-unreachable).

transaction.label: Transaction
transaction.doc: Implementation level: what one transition is atomic with respect to. Declarative; simulation ignores it.

refines.label: Refines
refines.doc: The model behavior this implementation behavior refines, through its refinement mapping (docs/claims-and-evidence.md, "Refinement").

refinement.label: Refinement mapping
refinement.doc: {states: {implState: modelState}, variables: {modelVar: expression over this behavior's variables}, transitions: {implTransition: modelTransition or null}}; null is a stutter.

timeScale.label: Time scale
timeScale.doc: Implementation time units per model tick: the refinement check reads the model's time as the trace time divided by it, and compares model timer delays multiplied by it. Default 1.

state.label: State
state.doc: A defined configuration within a behavior.

ignores.label: Ignored events
ignores.doc: Implementation level: events this state deliberately does not react to, which satisfies the completeness rule. Declarative; simulation ignores it.

transition.label: Transition
transition.doc: A declared change between states with a trigger, guard and effects.

otherwise.label: Otherwise
otherwise.doc: Implementation level: marks the last transition of a (from, on) group as the fall-through. Its meaning is the declaration-order rule; simulation ignores it.

faultOnly.label: Fault only
faultOnly.doc: The transition exists only when a fault of kind enable-transition activates it.

fault.label: Fault
fault.doc: A declared deviation that a scenario run can inject.

kind.label: Kind
kind.doc: duplicate-event: the event is delivered and delivered again "by" later (default 0), as an at-least-once message is redelivered when its sender stops between dispatch and acknowledgement. lose-event: the event is not delivered, as an at-most-once message is lost when its sender stops between commit and dispatch. retry-event: the event is delivered after "attempts" failed dispatches, delayed by the runtime's backoff (system.generation.retry). In a scenario that runs implementation-level machines each kind must be one the runtime can produce (fault.unrealisable, docs/semantics.md).

occurrence.label: Occurrence
occurrence.doc: 1-based occurrence of the event to affect. Omitted means every occurrence.

by.label: Delay by
by.doc: Logical ticks (format 1) or a duration (format 2). For duplicate-event: how much later the second delivery comes (default 0).

attempts.label: Failed attempts
attempts.doc: For retry-event: a positive integer, the failed dispatches before the one that delivers; the delay is the sum of the backoff waits after each (system.generation.retry).

realises.label: Realises failure mode
realises.doc: The failure mode this injection is an instance of. Not read by the simulation engine.

window.label: Window
window.doc: {at, until?}: durations; the fault acts only in [at, until).

environment.label: Environment
environment.doc: What a deployment target guarantees: clock skew, message behavior, storage durability, consistency, zones and regions. Each guarantee names its source.

source.label: Source
source.doc: The entity that justifies the value: a requirement or other claim, an assumption, an evidence entity, or an entity of any kind the specification declares. Required; a missing source is a validation error.

failureMode.label: Failure mode
failureMode.doc: One way a component, a relationship or an environment can fail, with a sourced rate and duration.

scope.label: Scope
scope.doc: How much fails together: one instance up to a whole provider.

rate.label: Rate
rate.doc: How often it happens. Required, with a source; a missing rate or rate source is a validation error.

source.label: Source
source.doc: The entity that justifies the value: a requirement or other claim, an assumption, an evidence entity, or an entity of any kind the specification declares. Required; a missing source is a validation error.

duration.label: Duration
duration.doc: How long it lasts. With a duration, a source is required.

source.label: Source
source.doc: The entity that justifies the value: a requirement or other claim, an assumption, an evidence entity, or an entity of any kind the specification declares. Required; a missing source is a validation error.

faultModel.label: Fault model
faultModel.doc: A named set of failure modes in an environment, with bounds on how many may occur at once. Claims are evaluated under a fault model.

scope.label: Scope
scope.doc: Limits failures of this scope. Omit to bound the listed modes (or all modes) regardless of scope.

source.label: Source
source.doc: The entity that justifies the value: a requirement or other claim, an assumption, an evidence entity, or an entity of any kind the specification declares. Required; a missing source is a validation error.

resource.label: Resource
resource.doc: A pool of identical units (CPU cores, I/O channels, connections, pool slots, threads) that behaviors use, acquire and release (format 2; docs/simulation.md, "Resources").

demandFactor.label: Demand factor
demandFactor.doc: A step table [[n, num, den], ...] or {usl: {alpha, beta}} with exact decimals.

source.label: Source
source.doc: Where the number comes from: {kind: requirement | measurement | assumed | to-be-measured, ref?, date?}.

link.label: Link
link.doc: A message link between two components: a FIFO transfer queue at a bandwidth, then a propagation latency (format 2; docs/simulation.md, "Links, payload size and bandwidth").

bandwidth.label: Bandwidth
bandwidth.doc: "<decimal> <unit>": bit/s, kbit/s, Mbit/s, Gbit/s, B/s, kB/s, MB/s or GB/s.

source.label: Source
source.doc: Where the number comes from: {kind: requirement | measurement | assumed | to-be-measured, ref?, date?}.

workload.label: Workload
workload.doc: Load generated from outside the behaviors: open arrivals, a closed population of clients, or a population of client behavior instances (format 2; docs/simulation.md, "Workloads").

source.label: Source
source.doc: Where the number comes from: {kind: requirement | measurement | assumed | to-be-measured, ref?, date?}.

requestClass.label: Request class
requestClass.doc: Requests measured from a start event to the first end event carrying the same key (format 2; docs/simulation.md, "Request lifecycle").

scenario.label: Scenario
scenario.doc: A specified sequence of input events and active faults executed over a set of behaviors.

tags.label: Tags
tags.doc: Labels for the scenario. generated-coverage marks a scenario that exegra cover-machines generated to exercise a transition or guard outcome the other scenarios leave out (docs/coverage.md).

faultModel.label: Fault model
faultModel.doc: The fault model this scenario's injected faults are drawn from.

timeUnit.label: Time unit
timeUnit.doc: Format 2: the base unit of times (default us).

assumption.label: Assumption
assumption.doc: A condition accepted by the model but not established by available evidence.

type.label: Type
type.doc: A declared data type a code generator maps: an identifier, a scalar over a built-in representation, an enumeration, a struct or a tagged union. Names that are not declared resolve only when they are built-in (src/core/builtin-types.js), list<T> / set<T> / option<T> / shared<T> of a type that resolves, or map<K, V> of a key and a value that resolve. A set<T> is a JSON array of distinct items, in order. A shared<T> is a sharing hint, identical to T on the wire.

repr.label: Representation
repr.doc: For an id or a scalar: the built-in representation type.

variants.label: Variants
variants.doc: For a union: its variants, each {name, fields?, newtype?, tuple?}. A variant without fields is a unit variant; newtype: true marks a variant with exactly one field that is written without the field's name (serde's newtype variant); tuple: true marks a variant with two or more positional fields, written as a JSON array of their values in order (serde's tuple variant, {"Cmp": ["Eq", a, b]}).

encoding.label: Wire encoding
encoding.doc: For a union: how a value is written. tag external (default): {"Variant": content}, a unit variant is the bare name; internal: the variant name is a member tagField of the object holding the fields; adjacent: {tagField: name, contentField: content}; untagged: the variant's own JSON with no name (a unit variant is null, a newtype its field's value, a tuple an array, any other variant an object of its fields), tried in declaration order when read. variantCase converts the variant names on the wire (as written when absent).

constraints.label: Constraints
constraints.doc: For an id or scalar: pattern (a regular expression, over a string representation), minLength and maxLength (over a string or bytes representation).

sensitive.label: Sensitive
sensitive.doc: The kind of sensitive data a value of the type is (a secret, a password, a token, personal data). A field of a sensitive type is never logged; a struct with a sensitive field, and list<T> or option<T> of a sensitive T, are sensitive too.

metamodel.label: Tenant metamodel role
metamodel.doc: The part of the tenant-schema metamodel this type is, in a system whose tenants describe their own data. tenant-schema: a tenant's schema, the root; object-id: the id of a tenant object type; field-id: the id of a field of one; values: the field values of one tenant record; definition: any other part (object, field, constraint, workflow, policy definitions). A record field of an object-id or values type, or a map keyed by a field-id type, carries tenant domain data (record.tenant-data-fixed).

language.label: Language
language.doc: An expression language that users of the specified system write (such as a tenant rule language), described so that a generator can produce its parser, printer, checker and evaluator: the AST and value unions, the static shapes, the scopes names are read through, and one operator per AST variant (or per case of one), each naming a primitive of the fixed catalogue in src/core/language.js. It is not Exegra's guard language and is not mirrored in Lean.

ast.label: AST
ast.doc: The union type of expressions; each variant is one expression form.

values.label: Values
values.doc: The union type of what an expression evaluates to.

shapes.label: Shapes
shapes.doc: The names of the static shapes the checker gives expressions.

anyShape.label: Any shape
anyShape.doc: The shape of null and of what the checker cannot pin down; it is accepted wherever another shape is expected.

scopes.label: Scopes
scopes.doc: How names are read: record-scope (<scope>.<field>, with system attributes), param (<scope>.<name>), constant (a bare word), role-test (<scope>(<role>)).

value.doc: For a record-scope: the value of the AST's scope field it stands for.

attributes.doc: For a record-scope: its system attributes, each {name, shape}; a name starts with $.

operators.label: Operators
operators.doc: One per AST variant, or one per case of one field of a variant: its syntax, operand and result shapes, null handling and primitive.

variant.doc: The AST variant it parses to and prints from.

case.doc: When a variant has one operator per value of one of its fields: that field (an enum or union) and the value.

precedence.doc: For a binary or prefix operator: a positive integer; higher binds tighter.

operands.doc: The shape of each operand: a shape name, or a list of the shapes it accepts.

result.doc: A shape name, or operand:<n> (1-based) for the shape of an operand.

primitive.doc: An entry of the primitive catalogue (src/core/language.js).

function.label: Function
function.doc: A pure function a generator compiles into code, such as a kernel's intent decision or policy evaluation: typed parameters, a return type, an optional union of errors, lets and a body in the function body language (src/core/function-syntax.js), and examples Exegra evaluates in JavaScript. The call graph is acyclic, so every function is total. Not mirrored in Lean.

params.label: Parameters
params.doc: Each {name, type}: a plain name and a type that resolves (or result<T, E>).

returns.label: Returns
returns.doc: The type of the value the body gives.

errors.label: Errors
errors.doc: The union type of the ways the function can fail; fail(...) gives one of its variants and try passes one on.

let.label: Lets
let.doc: Names bound in order before the body, each {name, expr}.

body.label: Body
body.doc: An expression of the function body language (docs/model-and-format.md, Functions).

examples.label: Examples
examples.doc: Each {args, result} or {args, error}: args an object of the parameters, result or error a JSON value (unions in serde's external form). Validation evaluates every example.

exampleFixture.label: Example fixture
exampleFixture.doc: A value declared once for the examples of functions: a tenant, a schema, a principal. An example argument, result or error is {fixture: <id>} or {fixture: <id>, with: {<dotted path>: <value>}}; Exegra resolves it before evaluating the example and a generator writes it once per fixture (docs/model-and-format.md, Example fixtures).

type.label: Type
type.doc: The type of the value: a type text that resolves, or result<T, E>. A fixture stands only where this type (or an option of it) is expected.

value.label: Value
value.doc: The value as examples write values (docs/model-and-format.md, Functions); it must be a value of the type.

record.label: Record
record.doc: A kind of record the system stores: its owning component, key, fields and retention. The data rules (src/core/data-model.js) are computed over records and their copies.

owner.label: Owning component
owner.doc: The component whose state this record is: the authoritative table.

key.label: Key
key.doc: Names of the fields that identify a record. Each must be a declared field.

type.label: Type
type.doc: Free type text such as principal-id, display-name, number or timestamp. A type containing the word name or handle counts as a name.

personal.label: Personal-data class
personal.doc: Set when the field is personal data of a principal.

classification.label: Classification
classification.doc: How sensitive the field is. The personal-data class above is the one way to say a field is personal: classification personal is accepted only together with a class, and a field with a class is not classified otherwise. credential is treated as personal by rule record-erasure-point.

refersTo.label: Refers to
refersTo.doc: The record this field holds the key of, or "principal" for a principal id.

role.label: Role
role.doc: party: a principal taking part in the act (must refer to the principal by id); subject: the principal the record is about; snapshot: a copy of a value as it was at the time of the act.

optional.label: Optional
optional.doc: True when a record may leave the field unset.

onDelete.label: On delete
onDelete.doc: What deleting the referred record does to this one. Only with refersTo; set-null needs optional.

unique.label: Unique
unique.doc: Sets of field names whose combined values are unique.

schemaVersion.label: Schema version
schemaVersion.doc: A positive integer: the version of the stored shape.

changes.label: Changes
changes.doc: One entry per schema version, 1 to schemaVersion.

retention.label: Retention
retention.doc: How long a record is kept and what ends it. Prose: the erasure property is what is checked.

point.label: Erasure point
point.doc: When a principal's deletion (or the end of the retention) has removed the record.

bound.label: Bound
bound.doc: How long after that point the record is removed, in the unit; a bounded retention.

basis.label: Basis
basis.doc: Why the record is kept beyond a deletion, when it is (a legal obligation, a financial record).

scope.label: Scope
scope.doc: Which side of a metadata model the record is on. platform: a fixed table of the platform, whose declared fields are its whole shape. tenant-meta: a fixed table of the platform whose rows carry tenant-defined data as data (generic records, the schema history), shaped at run time by the tenant schema named in describedBy. Tenant domain data is never a fixed record of its own (rule record.tenant-data-fixed). Required on every record once a type has metamodel tenant-schema (record.scope-missing).

describedBy.label: Described by
describedBy.doc: For scope tenant-meta: the type with metamodel tenant-schema whose values describe the rows' payload at run time (record.described-by).

realisation.label: Realisation
realisation.doc: shipped (default): the running system has this table as declared. target: a record of the target design that the running system does not have yet, kept for the machines that model it.

source.label: Source
source.doc: The entity that states this record (a requirement, decision or case).

copy.label: Copy
copy.doc: A place where some or all fields of one or more records are kept outside their owning component: a cache, a derived view, a CDN variant, a per-session store.

of.label: Copy of
of.doc: The record, or the records of a projection, that this copy holds fields of.

fields.label: Fields held
fields.doc: Field names of the source records, or record-id.field when ambiguous. Omitted: every field of every source record.

scope.label: Scope
scope.doc: shared: served as stored to more than one viewer (a CDN, a shared cache); per-session or per-principal: served only to one sign-in session or principal; internal: held server-side and never served as stored, every answer passing a read-time authority filter.

bound.label: Bound
bound.doc: How far an answer from this copy may trail its source: a number with a unit, or a text such as zero, K-62 or the read stamp.

point.label: Erasure point
point.doc: When a principal's deletion (or the end of the source record) has reached this copy.

basis.label: Basis
basis.doc: Why the copy is kept beyond a deletion, when it is (a legal obligation, a financial record).

dependsOnAuthority.label: Depends on authority
dependsOnAuthority.doc: True when the content of the copy depends on who is asking (grants, age band, privacy, blocks).

policy.label: Policy
policy.doc: Who may do what: a subject (principal kind and role) may or may not perform an action (a contract or a transition) on a resource (a record) when a condition holds. A matching deny refuses; otherwise a matching allow permits; otherwise the contract's policyDefault decides, and for a transition the default is deny (docs/model-and-format.md, "Cross-cutting constructs").

principal.label: Principal kind
principal.doc: The kind of principal, such as member, operator or service.

role.label: Role
role.doc: The role the principal holds; omitted means any role.

contract.label: Contract
contract.doc: The action, when it is a contract call. Exactly one of contract and transition.

transition.label: Transition
transition.doc: The action, when it is a transition of a behavior. Exactly one of contract and transition.

resource.label: Resource
resource.doc: The record acted on; its fields are record.<field> in the condition.

condition.label: Condition
condition.doc: A boolean expression over request.<input> (contract) or event.<field> (transition), record.<field> (with a resource), and principal.id, principal.tenant and principal.role.

source.label: Source
source.doc: The entity that states the policy, such as a requirement.

validation.label: Validation
validation.doc: One rule a value must meet before it is accepted: a contract input or a record field, a rule from a fixed set, and the message a refusal carries.

contract.label: Contract
contract.doc: With input: the target is that input of the contract. Exactly one of contract and record.

record.label: Record
record.doc: With field: the target is that field of the record.

maxLength.label: Maximum length
maxLength.doc: For rule maxLength: a positive integer.

unit.label: Length unit
unit.doc: For rule maxLength: what the length counts (Unicode scalar values, or bytes of UTF-8).

pattern.label: Pattern
pattern.doc: For rule pattern: a regular expression the whole value matches.

min.label: Minimum
min.doc: For rule range: the least value allowed.

max.label: Maximum
max.doc: For rule range: the greatest value allowed.

values.label: Values
values.doc: For rule oneOf: the values allowed.

expr.label: Expression
expr.doc: For rule custom: a boolean expression over value (the target) and request.<input> or record.<field>.

retention.label: Retention
retention.doc: How long records of one kind are kept and what happens then: keep for a duration or until an event, then delete, anonymise or archive. The structured form of the record's prose retention; the record's erasure still states what a principal's deletion does.

keepFor.label: Keep for
keepFor.doc: A duration "<decimal> <unit>" with ns, us, ms, s, min, h or d, counted from the record's creation. Exactly one of keepFor and until.

until.label: Until
until.doc: The event that ends the retention.

fields.label: Anonymised fields
fields.doc: For anonymise: the fields that are cleared.

archiveTo.label: Archive to
archiveTo.doc: For archive: the component that holds the archive.

quota.label: Quota
quota.doc: A limit on how often one scope may call a contract or produce an event in a window, and what happens beyond it.

contract.label: Contract
contract.doc: The counted resource, when it is a contract. Exactly one of contract and event.

event.label: Event
event.doc: The counted resource, when it is an event.

limit.label: Limit
limit.doc: A positive integer: how many in one window.

window.label: Window
window.doc: A duration "<decimal> <unit>" with ns, us, ms, s, min, h or d.

error.label: Error
error.doc: For refuse on a contract: the name of the contract error the refusal is.

heldBy.label: Counters held by
heldBy.doc: The component that keeps the counters.

retry.label: Retry
retry.doc: How a contract call or an emitted event is retried: attempts, backoff, the idempotency key that makes a repeat harmless, and the timeout of one attempt.

contract.label: Contract
contract.doc: The retried call. Exactly one of contract and event.

attempts.label: Attempts
attempts.doc: A positive integer: the most attempts, the first included.

base.label: Base
base.doc: A duration: the wait before the second attempt, and every wait when fixed.

cap.label: Cap
cap.doc: For exponential: the longest wait, a duration of at least the base.

idempotencyKey.label: Idempotency key
idempotencyKey.doc: An input of the contract, or a payload field of the event, that identifies repeats.

timeout.label: Timeout
timeout.doc: A duration: how long one attempt may take.

audit.label: Audit
audit.doc: An audit record written whenever a contract is called, a transition fires or an event occurs: the record kind written, the fields captured, and how the log is kept immutable.

contract.label: Contract
contract.doc: The trigger, when it is a contract call. Exactly one of contract, transition and event.

transition.label: Transition
transition.doc: The trigger, when it is a transition.

event.label: Event
event.doc: The trigger, when it is an event.

field.label: Field
field.doc: A field of the record written.

from.label: From
from.doc: An expression over request.<input> and response.<output> (contract), event.<field> (transition or event), principal.id, principal.tenant, principal.role and time.

immutability.label: Immutability
immutability.doc: append-only: entries are never changed or removed. chained-hash: append-only, and each entry holds the hash of the one before it in chainField.

chainField.label: Chain field
chainField.doc: For chained-hash: the field of the record that holds the previous entry's hash (bytes or string).

capability.label: Capability
capability.doc: A named thing a principal may do, which contracts require (auth.requires), plans entitle, roles and grants confer, delegations and token scopes pass on, and feature flags gate per tenant. A call is admitted only when the tenant's plan entitles every capability it requires (or the capability is core), no flag gating it is off for the tenant, the principal holds it, and a delegation it acts under passes it on (docs/model-and-format.md#capabilities-plans-and-roles).

core.label: Core
core.doc: True when every tenant has it whatever its plan: no plan needs to entitle it.

source.label: Source
source.doc: The entity that states it, such as a requirement.

plan.label: Plan
plan.doc: What a tenant buys: the capabilities beyond the core ones its tenants are entitled to.

capabilities.label: Capabilities
capabilities.doc: The ids of the capabilities the plan entitles.

role.label: Role
role.doc: A named set of capabilities held by principals. A platform role is the platform's own (operators, services, anonymous visitors): its capabilities are what the specification lists. A tenant role is one a tenant starts with: it is tenant data, the tenant may change it, and the capabilities listed are those it starts with.

level.label: Level
level.doc: platform: defined by the specification. tenant: a role a tenant starts with, held as tenant data.

holders.label: Holders
holders.doc: Who may hold it: people, platform services, agents, teams, anonymous callers, or external parties that prove themselves by signature or provisioning token.

capabilities.label: Capabilities
capabilities.doc: The ids of the capabilities it confers.

grant.label: Grant
grant.doc: Capabilities one role issues to holders of another for a bounded time, such as a support grant a tenant owner issues to platform support for one tenant. A grant passes on only capabilities its issuer holds (delegation.exceeds).

issuer.label: Issued by
issuer.doc: The role whose holders issue it.

grantee.label: Granted to
grantee.doc: The role whose holders receive it.

capabilities.label: Capabilities
capabilities.doc: The ids of the capabilities it confers while it lasts.

perTenant.label: Per tenant
perTenant.doc: True when each grant names one tenant and confers its capabilities in that tenant only.

maxDuration.label: Longest duration
maxDuration.doc: How long one grant may last at most, a duration such as "72 h".

delegation.label: Delegation
delegation.doc: Capabilities a principal passes on to another (an agent, a service) to act for it. The delegate holds at most the capabilities listed, and at run time at most those its delegator holds; the listed capabilities are within what its source holds (delegation.exceeds).

from.label: Delegated from
from.doc: What the delegator holds that the delegation is issued from: a role, a token scope, another delegation or a grant.

capabilities.label: Capabilities
capabilities.doc: The ids of the capabilities it passes on.

maxDuration.label: Longest duration
maxDuration.doc: How long one delegation may last at most, a duration such as "1 h".

tokenScope.label: Token scope
tokenScope.doc: A scope an access token is issued with: the capabilities a call made with the token may use, at most.

name.label: Name
name.doc: The scope as a token carries it, such as content:write.

capabilities.label: Capabilities
capabilities.doc: The ids of the capabilities it allows.

featureFlag.label: Feature flag
featureFlag.doc: A switch held per tenant that gates capabilities: while it is off for a tenant, nobody in that tenant may use them.

gates.label: Gates
gates.doc: The ids of the capabilities it gates.

default.label: Default
default.doc: Its value for a tenant that has no setting of its own; off when unstated.

screen.label: Screen
screen.doc: A page of the user interface: the route it answers, the contract whose response is its view model, and the hand-written renderer that draws it (docs/model-and-format.md, "User interface").

route.label: Route
route.doc: A path pattern: "/" or /segment/... where a segment is a literal or :param; or a catch-all, "*" or "*name", that answers every path no other screen answers (name: the route parameter holding that path). Route parameters are strings.

query.label: Query parameters
query.doc: Optional query-string parameters the screen reads, such as q of /search?q=.

viewModel.label: View model
viewModel.doc: The contract whose outputs are the screen's data. It is called with the route and query parameters as inputs of the same names.

kind.label: Renderer
kind.doc: The name of the hand-written renderer that draws the view model.

auth.label: Authentication
auth.doc: none, session (any signed-in principal) or role:<role>.

local.label: Screen-local values
local.doc: Values the screen holds besides its view model, each {name, type}, empty until an action places a call's output there (action.result); expressions read them as local.<name> and the renderer draws them.

form.label: Form
form.doc: A form on a screen whose submission calls a contract. Each field fills one input; the validation constructs on those inputs are the field checks, stated once.

label.label: Label
label.doc: The accessible name of the control.

options.label: Options
options.doc: For a select or radio: the choices, each {value, label}.

optionsFrom.label: Options from the view model
optionsFrom.doc: For a select or radio instead of options: path, a path into the screen's view model reaching a list; for a list of structs, value and label name the fields giving each option's value and label; for a list of strings each item is its own value and label.

derive.label: Derived from
derive.doc: An expression over the other fields (form.<field>) and the screen's scope that fills this field as they change.

until.label: Derived until
until.doc: edited: deriving stops once this field has been edited. Left out: always derived.

transform.label: Transform
transform.doc: A transform applied to the derived value. slug: Unicode NFKD, combining marks removed, lower case, every run of characters other than a-z and 0-9 replaced by -, - trimmed at both ends, cut to 80 characters, trailing - trimmed.

initial.label: Initial value
initial.doc: Where the field's value comes from when the form opens: path, a path into the screen's view model (a number is shown as text, a list of texts joined with join); with where, path reaches a list of structs and the field takes the value at path value of the first item whose where.field equals the expression where.equals. Nothing there: the control's own initial value.

equals.label: Equals
equals.doc: An expression over the screen's scope, such as principal.id.

value.label: Value field
value.doc: With where: the path in the item that gives the value.

join.label: Join with
join.doc: For a list of texts shown in a text control: the separator.

normalize.label: Normalize
normalize.doc: trim: the submitted text has white space removed at both ends before it is sent and before the outcome reads it.

arguments.label: Other inputs
arguments.doc: Contract input -> expression over route.<param>, view.<output> and principal, for the inputs no field fills.

then.label: Then
then.doc: A second call made when the first succeeds, before onSuccess: contract, with arguments (input -> expression over the outcome's scope: response.<output> of the first call, form.<field> and the screen's scope). It sends only the inputs it names. onSuccess then reads the outputs of both calls, the second's where both have one.

submitLabel.label: Submit label
submitLabel.doc: The accessible name of the submit button.

onSuccess.label: On success
onSuccess.doc: What the page does when the call succeeds: navigate to a screen (params: route parameter -> expression over response.<output>, route.<param>, view.<output> and principal), show a toast, or both.

params.label: Route parameters
params.doc: Route parameter -> expression; may also read query.<param> of the current screen and, on a form, form.<field>.

path.label: Address
path.doc: An expression of a string, such as query.next: the address opened when it is a same-site absolute path (starts with / and not //); otherwise the screen is opened.

toast.label: Toast
toast.doc: The text shown; ${response.<output>[.<field>]}, ${form.<field>}, ${item.<field>}, ${route.<param>}, ${query.<param>}, ${view.<output>[.<field>]}, ${local.<name>} and ${principal.<attribute>} are filled in.

view.label: View model until it is read again
view.doc: Output -> expression over the outcome's scope: outputs of the view model of the screen the success opens (navigate.screen, else this screen) that hold these values until that view model is read again, such as the version a save moved the record to.

onError.label: On error
onError.doc: Where a refusal is shown: inline (next to the form or control, field errors on their fields) or as a toast. Its wording is the errorMessages that apply.

prefix.label: Prefix
prefix.doc: Text put before the message of a refusal shown as a toast, such as "Not done. ".

announce.label: Announce
announce.doc: What is announced when a refusal is only about fields, such as "Some fields need attention.".

action.label: Action
action.doc: A button on a screen that calls a contract with arguments taken from the route, the view model and the principal. Shown only when the policies on its contract may permit the current principal.

label.label: Label
label.doc: The accessible name of the button.

form.label: Form
form.doc: A form on the same screen whose field values the action reads: its arguments and navigation may use form.<field>, typed like in the form.

forEach.label: For each
forEach.doc: A path to a list of structs in the screen's view model: the action is repeated once per row, and item.<field> is that row in its expressions and, as ${item.<field>}, in its label and confirmation.

arguments.label: Arguments
arguments.doc: Contract input -> expression over route.<param>, view.<output>, item.<field> (per-row) and principal.

confirm.label: Confirm
confirm.doc: When set, the action asks for a second press with this text before calling.

confirmAnnounce.label: Announced when armed
confirmAnnounce.doc: With confirm: what is announced when the first press asks for the second.

alsoOn.label: Also on
alsoOn.doc: The action is also offered on every other screen whose authentication is auth (a screen without one is none), such as a sign-out in the page's header. It then reads only principal and response.<output>.

optimistic.label: Optimistic
optimistic.doc: True when the page shows the success before the reply, and undoes it on a refusal.

result.label: Result
result.doc: Keep the call's result on the screen instead of navigating: output, an output of the contract, is placed in into, a screen-local value of the screen of the same type.

onSuccess.label: On success
onSuccess.doc: What the page does when the call succeeds: navigate to a screen (params: route parameter -> expression over response.<output>, route.<param>, view.<output> and principal), show a toast, or both.

params.label: Route parameters
params.doc: Route parameter -> expression; may also read query.<param> of the current screen and, on a form, form.<field>.

path.label: Address
path.doc: An expression of a string, such as query.next: the address opened when it is a same-site absolute path (starts with / and not //); otherwise the screen is opened.

toast.label: Toast
toast.doc: The text shown; ${response.<output>[.<field>]}, ${form.<field>}, ${item.<field>}, ${route.<param>}, ${query.<param>}, ${view.<output>[.<field>]}, ${local.<name>} and ${principal.<attribute>} are filled in.

view.label: View model until it is read again
view.doc: Output -> expression over the outcome's scope: outputs of the view model of the screen the success opens (navigate.screen, else this screen) that hold these values until that view model is read again, such as the version a save moved the record to.

onError.label: On error
onError.doc: Where a refusal is shown: inline (next to the form or control, field errors on their fields) or as a toast. Its wording is the errorMessages that apply.

prefix.label: Prefix
prefix.doc: Text put before the message of a refusal shown as a toast, such as "Not done. ".

announce.label: Announce
announce.doc: What is announced when a refusal is only about fields, such as "Some fields need attention.".

liveBinding.label: Live binding
liveBinding.doc: An event the backend publishes that refreshes an open screen: the whole view model, or one output of it.

refresh.label: Refresh
refresh.doc: whole, or a path into the view model: an output of the view-model contract, then fields of its struct types.

when.label: When
when.doc: Refresh only when this holds: an expression over event.<payload field> and the screen's scope, {value, in: view-model path} (the value is an item of that list), or {any: [...]} / {all: [...]} of such conditions.

errorMessage.label: Error message
errorMessage.doc: The wording of a refusal: for a failed check of a kind (on check) or for an error code (on error), for every form and action or for those it applies to (docs/model-and-format.md, "User interface").

on.label: On
on.doc: check: a failed check of the reply (its rule kind, such as required or constraint). error: the error code of the reply, when no failed check explains it.

kinds.label: Kinds
kinds.doc: The check kinds or error codes it words. Left out: every other one (the default).

text.label: Text
text.doc: On check: ${check.detail} (the detail as sent) and ${check.statement} (the detail without the bracketed reference at its end) are filled in. On error: ${error.message}.

fallback.label: Fallback
fallback.doc: The text when the filled-in text is empty.

field.label: Field
field.doc: On check: the form field the message is shown on. name: the field the check names (object.field); prefix: the field whose name starts the check's name (title for title_length). Left out: the form as a whole.

appliesTo.label: Applies to
appliesTo.doc: The forms and actions it words, before the messages for all. Left out: all of them.

uiScenario.label: User journey
uiScenario.doc: A user journey a generator turns into an end-to-end browser test: steps that act and expect, selecting elements by role and accessible name only.

browsers.label: Browsers
browsers.doc: Names of separate browser sessions; the journey starts in the first. Omitted: one session.

steps.label: Steps
steps.doc: Each step is an object with exactly one key, a step kind of src/core/ui-steps.js (STEP_KINDS): navigation, actions, expectations, network and API checks, cookies, captured values, emulation and layout. Elements are addressed by role and accessible name (or name pattern), heading level and within only.

claim.label: Claim
claim.doc: A precise statement about a property expected to hold, with an explicit evaluation mechanism.

faultModel.label: Fault model
faultModel.doc: The fault model this claim is evaluated under. A result states it in its scope.

realisation.label: Realisation
realisation.doc: For a requirement. construction: generated code guarantees it, and some claim whose models names it checks that. checked: hand-written code, checked by tests. operational: measured on a running deployment.

realisedBy.label: Realised by
realisedBy.doc: For a requirement: the cross-cutting constructs that realise it by construction. A construction requirement is satisfied by a claim whose models names it or by at least one construct here.

integrityRule.label: Integrity rule
integrityRule.doc: A consistency rule over the whole specification, in the rule language of src/core/integrity.js. Evaluated on every edit: a transaction that adds a violation of an error rule is refused. Proved or refuted in Lean by exegra prove-integrity.

severity.label: Severity
severity.doc: error: an edit may not add a violation; warning: violations are reported only.

rule.label: Rule
rule.doc: The formula, e.g. forall d : decision, forall x in d.closes, x.resolvedBy == d. Entity ids written as literals are not references: a rename does not rewrite them.

basis.label: Basis
basis.doc: The entities this rule rests on: decisions, requirements, claims.

evidence.label: Evidence
evidence.doc: An artifact supporting or contradicting a claim. Author-entered; never an evaluation result by itself.

supports.label: Supports the claim
supports.doc: Defaults to true. False marks contradicting evidence.

view.label: View
view.doc: A named projection of the model with explicit filter and display rules.

entityKinds.label: Entity kinds
entityKinds.doc: For the references projection: which kinds of entity to draw.

depth.label: Reference depth
depth.doc: For the references projection: how many reference hops around the focused entity to draw (1 to 3).

layout.label: Layout method
layout.doc: Presentation only. Default for this view; a viewer may choose another without changing the model.

reader.label: Reader
reader.doc: For the reader projection: the page, as blocks read top to bottom.

text.label: Text
text.doc: For a text block: the paragraph, in plain Markdown.

kind.label: Entity kind
kind.doc: For counts, table and list blocks: the kind of entity they read.

where.label: Where
where.doc: Conditions every entity shown must meet.

property.label: Counted property
property.doc: For a counts block: the property whose values are counted.

pattern.label: Pattern
pattern.doc: A case-insensitive regular expression tested against the text.

classify.label: Classify
classify.doc: Rules mapping a text property to a status value; the first matching pattern wins.

groupBy.label: Group by
groupBy.doc: A property, or a dotted path through references such as table.section.

status.label: Status
status.doc: Classify this column by the block's classify rules and show it as a status.

columns.label: Columns
columns.doc: For a table block; without columns the kind's first properties are shown.

titleProperty.label: Title property
titleProperty.doc: For a list block: the property shown as each item's title.

statusProperty.label: Status property
statusProperty.doc: For a list block: the property classified as each item's status.

facet.label: Facet
facet.doc: A property whose values become filter choices.

facetSeparator.label: Facet separator
facetSeparator.doc: Splits the facet text into several values, such as ", ".

hideWhenSet.label: Hide when set
hideWhenSet.doc: Entities with this property set are hidden until the reader asks to see them.

document.label: Document
document.doc: For a document block: the document id; without it, the first document.

ids.label: Entity ids
ids.doc: For a sections block: the sections or tables to show, in order.
